"Twenty-two weeks," Ishita said, circling the date on the calendar above her desk. "The entrance test is on 18 May."

Her friend Charu looked up from the bed. "That sounds like a lot."

"It's not. Watch." Ishita opened the syllabus. "Physics, chemistry, maths: forty-eight units total. I need the last four weeks only for revision and mocks. That leaves eighteen weeks for new units."

"So?"

"So forty-eight divided by eighteen is about two and a half. I'll do three units a week to leave a buffer." She wrote it on the chart: Week 1: units 1, 2, 3.

"And if you fall behind?"

"Then I'll know in week two, not in May."

Charu came over and looked at the neat columns. "I haven't even counted my weeks."

"Count them tonight," Ishita said.

How might Ishita have felt as she laid out the numbers?
qa.a: She seemed focused and quietly confident, reassured by turning a big exam into weekly targets.

qa.q: What else could Ishita add to the plan?
qa.a: She could add a weekly check every Sunday, marking units done, so any slip shows up early and can be caught up.

qa.q: How might Charu see Ishita's plan?
qa.a: Charu seems impressed and a little anxious, realising she has not even counted her own weeks.

In October last year, I realised I'd been "preparing" for the entrance exam for months without knowing if I'd finish. I'm Bhavna, and my plan until then was: study hard and hope.

My brother Arnab, who'd cleared the same test two years before, sat me down. "How many weeks till the exam?"

I counted on the calendar. Twenty-six.

"And how many units in the syllabus?"

I hadn't counted that either. It was fifty-four.

"Keep the last five weeks for revision and full mocks," he said. "Now do the maths yourself."

So I did. Twenty-one weeks for new work. Fifty-four units. About two and a half a week. I rounded up to three, so I'd have a little slack.

It sounds so simple written down. But for the first time, I could see whether I was on track each Sunday, instead of just feeling guilty every night.

qa.q: How many units were in Bhavna's syllabus?
How did Bhavna feel before making the weekly plan?
qa.a: Bhavna felt guilty every night and unsure whether the syllabus would be finished.

qa.q: What else could Bhavna add to the weekly plan?
qa.a: Bhavna could note on Sundays which units felt weak, so they get extra time in the revision weeks.

qa.q: How might Arnab see Bhavna's new plan?
qa.a: Arnab probably feels pleased and satisfied, since his questions led Bhavna to work out the numbers independently.
